speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative visit. Please describe the "shooting ear pain" you are experiencing; does it radiate to your jaw or temple, and is it triggered by touching the ear canal? Also, when you say you have difficulty wearing earrings, is this due to pain, a sensation of pressure, or a visible deformity of the earlobe or shell?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-tympanoplasty facial nerve palsy secondary to Bell's palsy or residual trauma.

I am not convinced by your diagnosis of "facial nerve palsy" as the primary cause of shooting ear pain and earring discomfort following a successful tympanoplasty. Your symptoms of pain while eating and difficulty with earrings point more toward a specific complication like a graft issue or neuroma rather than facial weakness. Let me clarify: does the pain in your ear occur specifically when you swallow or chew, and is the discomfort with earrings due to pain at the piercing site or a sensation of the shell being tight or misshapen?
